UPSTREAM: ifdtool: fix flumap handling in chipsets prior ibex peak/5 series The Upper Map section in the descriptor contains a database of flash chips (VSCC Table). Its offset is located at a fixed offset from the beginning of the image. ifdtool falsely calculates the offset from the descriptor signature which has moved by 16 bytes with step b of the Ibex Peak (5 series) chipset. This produces bogus output for all chipsets older than that. This patch corrects the behavior by calculating the offset of flumap by adding 4096 - 256 - 4 to the start of the image. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I6d51004f4cda98caa74577c524beb6c6504ca1e0 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 0d22614f468c0722d699a74e130ddbebe05c1798 Original-Change-Id: I14f029fe702c129dfd8069a58fbd41113700f7ef Original-Signed-off-by: Stefan Tauner <stefan.tauner@gmx.at> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/27858 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Arthur Heymans <arthur@aheymans.xyz> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1165160 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

cros-workon: drop cw_emake This wrapper existed to help recover incremental build failures on bots. The number of common.mk packages has declined significantly as we moved to platform2/gyp, and our bots have been moving to GCE (so the hostname check doesn't match) which means that logic doesn't kick in. Lets drop this to ease migration to a new common.mk eclass. If we still run into incremental errors, we can add logic outside the ebuild that nukes the caches for us.
